subject: Transportation Systems
title: Aerodynamics of Speed
description: A micro-lesson that makes Aerodynamics of Speed usable.

hook.text: Air resistance increases with the square of speed. Double the speed, quadruple the drag.

buildup.text: At 200 mph, over 80% of a train's energy fights air resistance—not rolling friction.

discovery.text: Smooth body panels, sealed gaps between cars, and tapered noses all reduce the drag coefficient.

twist.text: Two trains passing each other at speed create a pressure wave that shakes both. Spacing and timing matter.

climax.text: Every new generation of high-speed trains spends thousands of hours in wind tunnels before a single ride.

punchline.text: At high speed, the train's real enemy is the air itself.

quiz.question: What happens to air resistance when a train doubles its speed?
